newsitem.title: UK: France's CCCI aims to broaden Euromarket horizons.
newsitem.headline: France's CCCI aims to broaden Euromarket horizons.

text.p: Regular borrower Caisse Centrale du Credit Immobiler de France (CCCI) plans to issue new Eurobonds to build a stronger presence in the U.S. dollar market and achieve name recognition in Asia, representatives said at a news conference on Friday.

Target plans for CCCI -- the funding arm of Credit Immobilier de France (CIF) -- one of France's top providers of state-subsidised residential mortgages, include increasing its dollar allocation of debt to 35 percent from its present 15 percent.
It also aims to increase its distribution profile in the U.S. and Asia where currently investors are limited, and said it would have a "marketing approach to capital raising".
Thus far CCCI has launched 24 bonds in seven different currencies.
CCCI launched a $750 million seven-year Euro-Asian FRN on Friday which pays five basis points over three-month LIBOR.
"Bond sales are going well and we should meet our 25 percent Asian distribution target," general director Jean-Noel Destremau told Reuters.

"This issue is aimed at getting better name recognition among Asian and U.S. institutional investors and increasing our dollar allocation of bond debt which is currently underweight," he said, adding that the deal should provide a clear valuation of its credit.

Destremau said CCCI's commitment to the French franc sector would be pursued with annual issuance of around seven billion French francs ($1.2 billion) which will be achieved through around two issues per year.
CCCI last launched a 3.0 billion French franc December 2001 bond in February.

Destremau said CCCI future funding strategy took European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) into account and said it anticipated increased competition among borrowers, new pricing references and a greater focus on credits after EMU.
CCCI is also likely to launch a $2.0 billion Euro Medium Term Note programme later this year.
